deep_investigations.title: Anchor an Opentrons Heater-Shaker GEN1 on an OT2 deck
deep_investigations.category: Impact on AI timelines (unless importance gate explicitly fails)
deep_investigations.importance_exact_workflow: Laboratory automation technician equips an actual OT2 pipetting robot with its GEN1 orbital shaker. Anchoring is expressly required because shaking can dislodge the module. This is real robot commissioning, without borrowing a laboratory-worker employment total. Scope is deck installation only; it does not claim thermal operation or calibration.

components: GEN1 Heater-Shaker, manufacturer dimensions152×90×82mm and mass1.34kg; CNC aluminum/polycarbonate
Supported OT2 machined-aluminum ANSI/SLAS deck slot
GEN1 captive screw-driven lateral anchors shown in hs-anchors.png
Supplied T10 Torx screwdriver; ordinary tool cradle
hardware.starting_state: Robot power disconnected. Deck section fixed in authentic frame-equivalent support. Module loose on adjacent bench tray, anchors retracted. No module cables under the mounting feet. Driver separate. Software/calibration excluded.
hardware.interfaces: Module locating footprint128×86mm, screw-driven tabs extending laterally against deck retention surfaces. Actual manufacturer picture—not an arbitrary latch—defines the causal motion. Module sits before clamp force grows.
hardware.known: Product spec mass/material/nominal envelope, actual moduleJSON footprint and positional datum, actual OT2 deckDXF, tool type and manufacturer pull/rock criterion.
hardware.approximations: ModuleJSON envelope156.25×91.75 differs from bare product152×90; likely feature envelope but not verified. Treat156.25×91.75 conservatively for clearance. Simple nonfunctional housing approximation is allowed. Captive screw pitch/anchor dimensions/friction/driver dimensions need declared engineering choices and sensitivity checks; no OEM torque specification is asserted.
hardware.support: Authentic deck mounting boundary fixed to bench; does not immobilize module. No enlarged handles/hidden joints.
hardware.revision_caveat: Use GEN1 OT2 manual/moduleV1. Old OT2 repository deckRevA2 is historical CAD reference; compatibility with the exact current supplied deck is not proved. Do not substitute Flex caddy for OT2 deck or claim matched complete OEM revision.

deep_investigations.instruction: Install the Heater-Shaker GEN1 in the indicated OT2 deck slot. Tighten its anchors with the T10 driver, then put the driver down and leave the module secure with both hands clear.
deep_investigations.core_ability: Locate a relatively heavy instrument into a standardized shallow deck nest, then develop lateral anchor retention without lifting/cocking the housing.
deep_investigations.bimanual_challenge: One hand holds the module down and square while the second acquires/engages driver at a low side port and tightens each anchor. Support hand must relocate without obstructing next screw.

physical_scoring.partial: 0.25 module seated square on the intended support surfaces, anchors not yet gripping;0.5 one anchor visibly retains and module remains seated;0.75 all anchors engaged but physical retention test incomplete;1.0 only with all anchors retained, module remains seated after hands clear and gentle prescribed test passes. For final submission recompute tiers from actual final anchor state, not historically achieved seating.
physical_scoring.full: Proposed benchmark measurement: no more than0.5mm translation or1degree rocking after a3N horizontal pull in±X/±Y and3N upward pull at the supplied inspection point, hands off. These numeric tests are authored conservative bench criteria, NOT Opentrons torque/load specifications. If OEM hardware cannot be scored this way, revise before implementation.
physical_scoring.measurement: Photo of seating/anchor projection plus dial ruler/feeler and spring scale. End state and retained clamp load under physical contact model; not number of screwdriver turns or hidden anchor-complete flag.
physical_scoring.invalid: Damaged anchor/threads, wrong slot, deck dislodged, cable trapped underfoot, or module held by robot yields0.

deep_investigations.reset: Back off anchor screws, remove module, inspect retention feet/threads, place anchors retracted and module/driver back on tray. No consumables.
incorrect_solutions_blocked: Resting module in its pocket without anchors: pull test fails; no full score.
Tighten only nearest anchor and cock opposite corner: all-anchor observation and multidirectional rock test fail.
Hold module down during test: explicit hands-clear condition fails.
Move/prop the deck or wedge foreign objects under module: intact named-fixture and foreign-object checks invalidate.

deep_investigations.core_ability: Build a rotating hollow bearing support around an already routed harness while preserving axial retention and cable clearance.
deep_investigations.bimanual_challenge: Counterhold small rear case, orient concentric parts around cable and seat the retaining cap/fasteners; reverse requires button release plus lifting hooks while retaining loose part.

physical_scoring.partial: 0.25 bearing seated and unpinched cable;0.5 bearing+idler correctly nested;0.75 cap captured but rotational inspection incomplete;1.0 retained stack rotates through its actual allowed travel without cable pinch and survives a declared gentle axial check after hands release. No credit for mere coaxial proximity.
physical_scoring.full: Observe complete bearing seating/cap engagement/required bolt heads and motion under a calibrated light force; choose numeric retention and running-torque thresholds only after actual drawing/hardware-backed mechanism specification. No sourced performance thresholds currently available.
physical_scoring.measurement: Calipers/close photo and spring-scale rotational/axial test; cable continuity plus physical jacket inspection.
physical_scoring.invalid: Fracture, crushed cable/connector, omitted bearing, foreign prop or unsupported force separation invalidates.

deep_investigations.reset: Remove retention fasteners and release actual cap hooks using manufacturer method; remove bearing/idler, inspect cable/jacket and hooks, return named parts. Replace damaged parts.
incorrect_solutions_blocked: Glue cap or jam cable to simulate retention: forbidden foreignmaterial and free-rotation/cable test fail.
Capture cap without bearing: visible part inventory and rotation test fail.
Leave assembly held by robot: hands-clear retention test fails.
Pull cable through/leave connector trapped: jacket/continuity and path inspection fail.

deep_investigations.title: Assemble the elastomer-centred optical foot contact switch of an ODRI quadruped
deep_investigations.importance_exact_workflow: ODRI explicitly designed this foot contact switch for its quadruped research robot. A robot builder assembles a floating foot aperture, optical emitter/receiver and compliant centring elements so foot contact changes the sensor signal. This is real legged-robot hardware construction; it does not borrow a general assembler employment count or relabel a generic pushbutton. It is assembly rather than encoder installation, calibration or an electrical test alone.

hardware.named_revision: ODRI Foot Contact Switch v1 / Lower Leg v1 drawing dated2019-10-07, source commit66af1522b4fba0ec4a1d7790e66f5e4652208d30. Do not mix a later Solo foot or different leg revision.
parts: 12 silicone tube segments, each6mm OD /4mm ID /3mm long, six on each side; source says these centre the foot
SLA printed foot structure, Accura Extreme Gray,3.4g; source STL bounds26.9995×27×16.5mm
FDM or SLS lower-leg structure base,18g; source STL bounds181×26.9945×20mm
FDM or SLS lower-leg fork,5g; source STL bounds62.5×16.7818×13.5mm
Two prewired optical electronics boards, each10mm diameter; source photo lists electronics2g total
M2.5×6 socket-head screws and existing M2.5×3.75 Helicoils at actual fork attachment points; source does not prescribe an assembly torque
Already bonded65×10mm Schwalbe Lugano23-622 tread on the foot. Bonding the tread is a prior subassembly, outside this task.
hardware.starting_state: Base on a nonblocking bench support, fork separate, foot/tread/pin already assembled as an authentic subassembly, optical boards already wired and electrically checked. All12 precut silicone annuli loose in a divided parts tray. Required closure screws separate or captive only if actual source hardware supports that state. No sensor element is preattached by a hidden simulator constraint.
hardware.mating_surfaces_and_retention: Source component photo and working-principle cutaway show six silicone elements around each side of the floating aperture. The lower-leg base and fork capture the foot/boards. The guided steel pin prevents foot rotation while the foot can deflect up to2mm. Actual source STEP/STL defines the pockets, aperture, support and pin path. Silicone contact forces—not a reset-to-centre script—must provide centring.
hardware.ordinary_tools_and_support: Ordinary electronics tweezers are a plausible manipulation aid for6×3mm annuli; their use is a proposed bench implementation choice, not a claimed source instruction. Stock YAM hands would acquire their normal handles. An ordinary small hex driver closes the real fork. A nest may support the long leg but cannot capture the loose foot or precompress the elements for the robot.
hardware.known_vs_approximate: Sizes/materials/masses above and3D geometry are explicit author sources. Source specifies10g foot/sensor/silicone assembly and35g whole lower leg. Exact silicone compound/hardness, compression/friction curve, tweezer dimensions, screw effort and assembly insertion forces remain unknown. These may be disclosed physical approximations, with sensitivity checks. The complete capture path and whether tweezers can release each piece inside the27mm foot are unresolved feasibility issues. The source gives a component overview and CAD, not a numbered twelve-element work instruction; the proposed order must be verified against that assembly, not presented as an OEM quote.

deep_investigations.instruction: Assemble the ODRI foot contact switch using all12 silicone centring elements and the prewired optical boards. Fit and secure the fork around the foot, keep the guide pin in its channel, then leave the foot centred, free to deflect and able to return after contact.
deep_investigations.core_ability: Capture distributed small compliant elements around a floating, optically active aperture, preserving multi-direction contact travel and passive return while closing a surrounding structure.
deep_investigations.bimanual_challenge: One arm supports and orients the leg/foot without losing the first bank of annuli; the other places and releases the second bank using an ordinary precision tool. Closure must not pinch a wire, shear an annulus or displace the antirotation pin. The support grasp must migrate so the fork can approach and the real fasteners remain accessible.

physical_scoring.partial: Proposed endpoint tiers:0.25 for one complete bank of six elements genuinely retained in their source pockets with the intact foot supported;0.5 for both banks and correctly oriented optical boards captured without a pinched cable;0.75 for the fork fully retained and the pin correctly guided but function not yet demonstrated;1.0 only after the full mechanical/optical outcome passes after the robot lets go. Any tier requiring an unstable loose state must be removed if the authentic assembly cannot retain it. Credits are final physical states, not historic insertion counts.
physical_scoring.full: All12 specified annuli remain captured, the pin prevents gross rotation, and the foot moves from neutral toward contact through the source-described travel up to2mm without hard binding, then returns. The actual3.3V optical circuit shows a reversible output change when a small external load moves the aperture, and returns to its baseline when unloaded. Source states analogue output spans3V to0V and LED divider threshold2.2V; do not claim force calibration from a geometry flag.
physical_scoring.proposed_measurement: Record close photos of both banks before closure and an end photo of the assembled, intact fork; inspect any obscured elements by source-supported witness openings or documented post-trial disassembly. Use a dial indicator or macro video scale for foot travel, a small spring scale for applied load, and a voltmeter or the actual board LEDs for reversible optical response. Initial benchmark choices such as neutral return error≤0.2mm and three load directions within the source270degree sensitivity sector are authored criteria, not manufacturer tolerances. Select a source-consistent force from the published force/output curve and state it; no numerical force threshold is claimed to have been extracted here.
physical_scoring.invalid: Missing or cut annuli, a cracked printed structure, adhesive replacing the elastic supports, omitted/unguided pin, crushed wiring, wrong board orientation or a foot held at neutral by the robot receives0. The circuit must remain low-voltage; mains/robot operation is not part of this task.
physical_scoring.fidelity: Contact/deformation of the actual tube segments and the floating aperture must cause travel/return. A localized deformable-ring or unilateral compliant-contact approximation is defensible if it allows slip, loss and asymmetric centring and is checked against the author curve. Rigid annuli joined to the foot or an angle/proximity-triggered green LED would erase the essential skill. Simplified optics may map actual aperture overlap to light intensity with declared parameters; no hidden installed flag.

deep_investigations.reset: Remove actual fork fasteners, separate the fork with the foot supported, recover all12 annuli, inspect for permanent set or cuts, inspect the pin/pockets/wires, return the preassembled tread/pin foot and prewired boards to their initial supports. Replace damaged annuli with the same6/4×3mm silicone stock. No pretend reversible bonding step.
incorrect_solutions_blocked: Omit several annuli and jam the foot against one wall: all12 inventory plus multidirectional passive travel/return fails.
Align the foot at neutral with a gripper while leaving the fork unretained: hands-clear retained-fork and external-load test fails.
Use adhesive, rigid shims or hidden fixed constraints to centre it: source inventory and reversible compliant motion fail.
Install boards backwards or cover the aperture with an annulus: actual optical voltage/LED response fails even if the housing looks complete.
Ignore the pin or trap a wire under the fork: pin guidance/rotation and cable/intactness inspections fail.

deep_investigations.parked_history_distinction: Our retired battery cross-key preload task#1733 captured a shared large spring preload with a transverse key in an invented pack fixture. This is not resurrected as a new sensor label: ODRI publishes the exact robot foot geometry, component photo, silicone dimensions, optical working principle and measured response. It has no battery, shared axial compression key or battery-storage claim. Distributed compliant insertion still carries its own fidelity risk.

YAM.scale_mass: Foot27mm diameter and16.5mm thick; annuli6mm OD×3mm long,12 total. Foot/sensor assembly≈10g, whole leg35g. Payload/reach are easy in planning; acquisition and access dominate.
YAM.grasp_and_tools: Stock fingertips approximately14mm wide are much larger than an individual6mm annulus. Ordinary precision tweezers held by the YAM are plausible; no oversized annuli, custom robot fingertips or enlarged pocket hardware. Tool handle acquisition, tip closure and part release need a real full-sequence check.
YAM.support_and_collision: The181mm leg provides a real external support grasp, but the second arm and tweezer shaft must clear the27mm circular foot and first installed bank. Check palm/wrist/second-arm/tool and all315 arm collision hulls; a fingertip reaching one pocket proves little.
YAM.planning_vs_verified: Only source documents/illustrations and STL vertex bounds were inspected. No YAM CPU IK/contact/clearance, tweezer wrench or physical return test ran. High risk is explicit.

hard_blockers: No demonstrated complete stock-YAM/tweezer path for placing and releasing12 annuli, retaining both banks and closing the fork.
Actual silicone deformation and part loss cannot be replaced by fixed springs or hidden install flags. Geometry source is complete; material exactness alone is not an automatic blocker.
deep_investigations.cheapest_falsification: Before a full material model, use the actual27mm foot and fork STL/STEP plus an ordinary tweezer envelope to check one deepest6mm annulus pocket, its release withdrawal and the opposing support grasp with full YAM hulls. Then test whether one bank stays in the genuine pockets as the other side is assembled. Reject if the real sequence needs a third hand or a custom oversized hand tool. Only after that implement one source-sized silicone annulus and test compliance/retention against the published curve.
deep_investigations.relative_effort: HIGH. Genuine complete geometry and a small mass help, but12 small compliant components plus precision-tool interaction make this costlier than the rigid Faze4 or ordinary fastener tasks. Keep as a defensible reserve, not a source-gated placeholder or a claimed quick win.

strongest_adversarial_rejection.rejection: The sensor is real, but12 tiny annuli inside a27mm foot cannot be assembled by normal YAM hands without a hidden helper; rigid approximations would turn the meaningful compliant mechanism into a peg-counting exercise.
strongest_adversarial_rejection.response: Primary mechanism/importance/geometry are established; full tool/contact-sequence and compliant retention remain to be falsified cheaply. No completed-demo or clearance claim.

deep_investigations.title: Tune the paired screws of a CELLO leader-arm drum brake to hold its load without excessive drag
deep_investigations.classification: BUILD-READY FOR CPU PREFLIGHT (source-guided only; kill if loose brake already holds or hold/backdrive window is empty)
deep_investigations.importance_exact_workflow: The CELLO designer explicitly builds a real GELLO teleoperation leader for the Franka Emika Panda. The source says stock springs/bands degrade and joints sag; CELLO uses non-decoupling passive brakes to make links stay put while preserving encoder synchrony. The actual build note instructs tightening both M3×25 preload screws symmetrically until the link holds its own weight with minimal drift while still moving smoothly. This is actual robotics data-collection/control hardware commissioning, not an invented generic service-arm occupation or an encoder-zero procedure. The designer reports more than a month of use in upstream hardware PR22; that is a source claim, not our hardware validation.

source_provenance.upstream_status: OPEN, seven commits; exact author fork source was read, not treated as merged upstream hardware
source_provenance.exact_instruction: Tune each brake by tightening both M3×25 preload screws symmetrically until the link holds its own weight with minimal drift while still driving smoothly.
source_provenance.source_limit: Full linked Google assembly guide is403. That does not block this tuning-only operation because the actual tuning instruction, materials, screw type, brake count/joint assignment and source assembly geometry are in the author GitHub README/STEP. Start with an authentic assembled brake, not an invented undocumented spring-installation sequence.
source_provenance.license: MIT License preserved from author fork; actual file credits Philipp Wu2023. Preserve attribution and note derivative CELLO authorship.

hardware.exact_revision: CELLO Franka/Panda passive-braked hardware at pinned commit. Choose the axial L1–L2 brake explicitly assigned by the source; do not mix original GELLO trigger parts, newer FR3 parts or different rotor/brake variants.
actual_components: Actual CELLO L1/L2 joint and specified downstream leader links, motors, handle/gripper and cabling; source link geometry is available. The actual downstream arm supplies the gravitational load, not an added counterweight or arbitrary test weight.
One axial split-drum brake: inner PETG rotor, two TPU95A pad segments and two PETG outer half-shells, all five actual solids in Brake Axial.step.
Two M3×25 symmetric preload screws at the source clamp ears; existing mounting screws hold the inner rotor/outer housing to their actual links.
Ordinary appropriately sized hex driver, tool cradle, nonblocking fixture using the real upstream link mounting interface.
Spring scale and ruler/protractor or optical angle tracker for external outcome checks; these are inspection instruments, not robot hand modifications.
hardware.source_measured_geometry: OCP/CadQuery imported the actual STEP as five solids. Inner rotor contact cylinder radius12.5mm. TPU pads have cylindrical radii12.6 and14.6mm, axial thickness8mm, individual bounds28.1946×10.7059×8mm. Outer split-shell contact radius14.7mm and outer radius24.7mm; each half bounds49.4×23.45×10.5mm. Overall nominal brake diameter49.4mm and axial thickness10.5mm. The two3.2mm clamp screw bores run parallel to the split-closing direction with axes at X±19.7mm. Rotor mounting holes are3.2mm diameter on source positions±4.9851mm. These are actual STEP surface/bounds observations, not OEM tolerances.
hardware.link_geometry: Actual L1 STEP bounds39.5×37.494×119.953mm; L2 bounds45.25×82.5×24mm. Bounds do not establish registered complete-arm poses or grasp clearance. Further links are present in the same source tree but no assembled full-arm pose was reconstructed.
hardware.material_mass: Designer specifies PETG structures/shells and TPU approximately Shore95A pads. Pad friction, compression/hysteresis, printing anisotropy, actual screw torque and loaded-arm mass/COM were not measured. Source volumes permit later mass estimates with disclosed density; they are not weighed hardware values. Do not take software/URDF placeholder masses as physical evidence.
hardware.initial_state: Actual preassembled L1–L2 joint in a reproducible real-arm pose with its axis horizontal and authentic downstream links producing a gravity moment. Both brake screws start backed off by a documented reproducible amount, with pads retained but brake drag below the required hold threshold. Downstream arm rests on a removable ordinary bench support until acquired. No encoder calibration or model motion occurs.
hardware.real_load_path: Inner rotor belongs to one link; split outer shells to the other. The two screws draw the outer half-shells symmetrically onto real TPU pads, producing normal force and circumferential friction against the inner drum. This friction acts in parallel with the rotational joint; it is not a clutch in series with the motor/encoder drive. Exact part labels and mounting registration must be carried from source geometry before implementation.
hardware.support_and_tools: Fixture reacts through actual upstream link/base mounting surfaces. One YAM supports an accessible genuine downstream link/handle while the other engages each M3 screw. No enlarged bolt heads, custom YAM fingertips, hidden hold or added counterweight. Tool size/handle geometry and nest dimensions are ordinary disclosed choices.

deep_investigations.instruction: Support the CELLO leader arm and adjust the two preload screws of the indicated axial brake evenly. Leave it holding its own weight at the marked pose, while the joint can still be moved smoothly by hand. Put the driver down and release the arm.
deep_investigations.core_ability: Adjust actual symmetric split-drum pad compression to create a bounded rotary friction torque: enough to resist the arm gravity moment, but low enough for smooth teleoperation.
deep_investigations.bimanual_challenge: One hand continuously supports the authentic loaded downstream chain to avoid a drop while the other applies a driver to two opposed clamp screws. The hands must exchange or relocate support to reach the second screw without bracing the brake during its final gravity/drag checks. Unequal tightening can cock the split shells or concentrate pad compression.

physical_scoring.principle: Score the final retained mechanical friction outcome after release, not screw angle, commanded torque or an installed flag. Both static hold and reversible rotary movement must pass at the same unchanged screw setting.
physical_scoring.partial: Proposed:0.25 if the real joint holds the loaded arm after release within the declared drift band at the test pose;0.5 if it holds at two source-reachable poses but the movement test fails or is incomplete;1.0 only if static hold and the bounded movement test both pass with the same setting and both clamp sides remain correctly seated. If a joint merely freezes because its pads are overclamped, it earns at most the static-hold tier. No credit for historical holds that are subsequently undone.
physical_scoring.full: Use an actual repeatable gravity-loaded pose and measure angular drift after hands clear. Then a standard external inspection applies a spring scale at a declared point on the real link and sweeps the joint slowly in both directions over a source-reachable angular interval. Measure tangential force times actual lever arm to obtain breakaway/running torque after accounting for gravity. The brake must hold again after the sweep without screw readjustment, binding or damage.
physical_scoring.numeric_bench_proposals: An initial bench specification might use angular drift≤2degrees over5s at two poses, a60degree total slow sweep, and maximum operator force≤2N at a real100mm lever point if such a point exists on the actual arm. These are explicit benchmark design proposals, NOT designer tolerances or verified achievable values. Use actual source geometry to select the lever point and load before implementation. A source-consistent torque window must exist between measured gravity torque and acceptable manipulation effort; if it does not, reject.
physical_scoring.symmetry_measurement: Photo/feeler measurement of the source split gaps at the two screw ears can check symmetric compression. A proposed maximum gap difference0.25mm must be checked against actual print geometry. Do not use equal screw-turn counts as a substitute for actual pad seating/torque outcome.
physical_scoring.invalid: Fractured PETG, cut/extruded TPU pads, stripped screw/nut, moved fixture, a foreign shim, disabled/removed actual drive parts, arms still supporting the chain or a changed screw setting between tests yields0. A robot may support the arm during adjustment but receives no static-hold credit while doing so.
physical_scoring.fidelity: Retain the actual split shells, pad surfaces and inner drum. Thread advance may use disclosed causal screw-joint coupling, but screw motion must physically compress pads and change normal force. Coulomb/Stribeck friction with declared TPU/PETG parameters is a normal engineering approximation; a setting-to-hold-torque lookup or hidden stiff joint is not. Modelling the pads as suitably compliant bodies with slip/release and shape-preserving contact is the central fidelity task. No exact material testing is falsely claimed.

deep_investigations.reset: Support the real downstream chain, back off both preload screws to a measured source-consistent split-gap start, confirm the initial arm no longer passes the hold criterion, return the authentic chain to its marked starting pose and ordinary support, and park the driver. Inspect pads and screw threads; replace damaged pads with the same printed material/revision. No consumables unless damaged.
incorrect_solutions_blocked: Tighten both screws until the joint is effectively seized: static hold alone receives partial credit; measured bidirectional breakaway/running-torque test fails.
Tighten only one ear so the housing cocks or pads extrude: actual split-gap/pad-seating check and smooth full-interval sweep fail.
Hold the arm or leave it propped on the support: explicit hands/support-clear gravity test fails.
Change screw setting between the static and drag tests: marked screw/gap state must remain unchanged; otherwise no full score.
Add a counterweight or relocate/remove actual arm parts to eliminate gravity load: named genuine hardware/inventory and COM/load inspection invalidate.
Rely on motor gear stiction or fixture friction with screws still loose: initial loose-brake baseline must fail the hold test, preventing a do-nothing full score.

competitors.legitimate_semantic_comparison: Service arm shifts a counterweight to cancel a gravitational moment, then captures alignment with a transverse pin. CELLO leaves the gravity moment present and adjusts dry rotary friction so an actual robot leader joint resists it while remaining backdrivable. No sliding counterweight, alignment holes or crosspin. Real teleoperation hardware/author build note establishes direct AI importance missing from the old invented generic service arm. This is not a revised title for that mechanism.

YAM.scale_and_grasps: 49.4mm brake is within nominal stock gripper span; source L1/L2 widths39.5/45.25mm provide plausible real support grasp regions. That is planning plausibility only. The whole genuine downstream chain and motors create unknown load/COM; verify payload and required holding torque before claiming feasibility.
YAM.driver: Ordinary M3-compatible hex driver acquired by its handle. Screw bores at X±19.7mm mean alternating low side approaches around a compact body. Driver engagement and wrench capacity require full contact/grasp checks; gripper force alone does not prove transmitted torque.
YAM.collision_and_support: Check palm, wrist, elbow, second arm, whole folded leader chain and driver against all315 collision hulls per arm. Full source-frame registration of the actual L1–L2 chain remains necessary. A source-sized brake cylinder alone is not a valid successful clearance test.
YAM.executed: Imported original5-solid STEP with CadQuery/OCP; measured per-solid bounds, cylindrical contact radii and hole axes; inspected actual unmodified geometry render. No YAM reach/collision, force, screw or pad simulation was run.

hard_blockers: Loose-brake baseline must actually sag under the genuine source arm load; if motor/gear stiction already meets full hold, the task is invalid without changing its authentic scope.
A feasible torque window between holding gravity and smooth operator movement must be demonstrated using actual source hardware/declared approximation; no fabricated torque threshold.

No complete simultaneous support/driver path has been verified. Source CAD is complete enough for a finite check; the missing Google assembly guide does not justify inventing a different initial joint assembly.
These are preflight kill conditions, not executed failures. No full-score or cleared-path claim is made.
deep_investigations.cheapest_falsification: First use the actual CELLO joint/leader configuration or a source-consistent mass/friction model to test loose-brake sag and a nonempty static-hold/running-torque window. Next register the source L1/L2 brake mount and run CPU full-hull clearance for both driver axes plus a stable real-link support grasp. Stop if it requires new oversized handles, added loads, moving the joint to a non-source interface or an unheld free chain beyond YAM capacity. Then simulate one source pad/contact pair with screw advance and friction, not the entire arm.
deep_investigations.relative_effort: MEDIUM/HIGH. The core has5 supplied solids,2 screws and ordinary rotary friction rather than belts, cable routing or twelve tiny silicone pieces. Source geometry and actual tuning instruction substantially reduce discovery cost. Material friction, actual chain registration and the test window remain material engineering work.

strongest_adversarial_rejection.rejection: This repeats the old preload/low-drag reasoning and substitutes another mechanism without proving actual gravity-loaded behaviour; the supplied servo may already hold the arm, making the task trivial.
strongest_adversarial_rejection.response: Specific physical skill, object setting and completed function differ from carriage stiffness, belt tension and counterweight balance. Actual designer procedure/geometry establishes importance/authenticity. The baseline/load-window objection must be falsified; no finished demo or clearance is claimed.
strongest_adversarial_rejection.independent_critic_verdict: No exact duplicate established. V-wheel lateral preload/rolling drag differs from rotary gravitational hold plus backdrive friction. Shared adjust/test tradeoff is insufficient under Version21. Authentic designer README resolves generic-service-arm importance, but does not permit a surrogate link or made-up load. Proceed only to source-guided CPU/preflight with sag/window kill conditions; actual TPU compression and symmetric screws must cause torque.
